Title: 'Verwandlung gemeiner Brüche in Decimalbrüche' (conversion of common fractions into decimal fractions); archive marks 'Math. 17', folio 15. The page is a table, not a derivation. For each odd denominator N up to 81 that is a prime or prime power (other than powers of 2 and 5), Gauss writes the repeating period of a/N. He writes one representative period for each orbit of the numerators under multiplication by 10 mod N, i.e. one per coset of the subgroup <10> in (Z/N)^*. Each period is copied out once, usually starting at the first nonzero digit (the leading 0 of 1/N is shifted to the end). He then repeats the first few digits, underlined, to mark the cyclic return. Parenthesised numbers in the left margin give the numerator a that produces the period on that line. This is the material of Disquisitiones Arithmeticae arts. 312-318 and Table III. The previous page (primes 409-439) shows the bundle is an extended working table of the same kind.

Entries, with ord = multiplicative order of 10 mod N:
- N = 3: 1/3 = 0.(3).
- N = 7: 1/7 = 0.(142857), ord 6.
- N = 9: 1/9 = 0.(1).
- N = 11: 1/11 = 0.(09), ord 2. The other four classes are not written.
- N = 13: ord 6, two classes. 1/13 = 0.(076923), written 769230...; 2/13 = 0.(153846).
- N = 17: 1/17, period 16, written 5882352941176470|588235.
- N = 19: period 18, written 526315789473684210|5263.
- N = 23: period 22, written 4347826086956521739130|4.
- N = 27: 1/27 = 0.(037), written 370370370. Only one of the six classes is given.
- N = 29: period 28, written 3448275862068965517241379310|344.
- N = 31: ord 15, two classes: 1/31 = 0.(032258064516129) and 3/31 = 0.(096774193548387).
- N = 37: ord 3, twelve classes, starting 027, 054, 081, 135, 162, 189, 243, 297, 378, 486, 459, 567 (numerators 1, 2, 3, 5, 6, 7, 9, 11, 14, 18, 17, 21). One crossed-out entry.
- N = 41: ord 5, eight classes needed. He lists 24390, 48780, 29268, 12195, 19512, 46341, 17073, 56097.
- N = 43: ord 21, two classes: 1/43 = 0.(023255813953488372093) and, marked (2), 2/43 = 0.(046511627906976744186).
- N = 47: period 46: 2127659574468085106382978723404255319148936170|21276 'cet.'
- N = 49: period 42: 2040816326530612244897959183673469387755|1020408.
- N = 53: ord 13, four classes, for numerators 1, (6), (12), (19): 1886792452830, 1132075471698, 2264150943396, 3584905660377.
- N = 59: period 58, written in four lines ending ...10169491.
- N = 61: period 60. The marginal (23) marks the line starting 377049..., which is 23/61.
- N = 67: ord 33, two classes: 1/67 and (7) 7/67 = 0.(104477611940298507462686567164179).
- N = 71: ord 35, two classes: 1/71 and (11) 11/71 = 0.(15492957746478873239436619718309859).
- N = 79: ord 13, six classes, numerators 1, (12), (9), (13), (29), (24): 1265822784810, 1518987341772, 1139240506329, 1645569620253, 3670886075949, 3037974683544.
- N = 81: ord 9. He gives 1/81 → 123456790, 2/81 → 246913580, 3/81 = 1/27 → 037, 4/81 → 49382716|493. The table continues on the next page with 5/81, 7/81, 8/81.

Implicit method (my reconstruction): long division, together with the facts that the period of a/N is the period of 1/N multiplied by a, and that rotating a period gives the period of 10^k·a/N. This is why one period per coset of <10> suffices.
errors: N = 41: 19512 is a cyclic rotation of 12195 (5/41 and 8/41 lie in the same class), so one class is listed twice.
N = 41: the class of 15/41 = 0.(36585) (rotations 36585, 65853, 58536, 85365, 53658) is missing, so only 7 of the 8 classes appear.
N = 73 (1/73 = 0.(01369863), ord 8, nine classes) is omitted between 71 and 79, and does not appear at the top of the next page either.
N = 81: 4/81 has period 049382716. Rotated it should read 493827160|493; the page shows 49382716 493, apparently dropping the 0.
N = 59, third line: the correct digits are 4576271186440677966. The image may read ...677926 here, which would be a digit slip; this is uncertain.
Incompleteness rather than error: N = 11, 9 and 27 show only one class although several exist; N = 81 includes 3/81 = 1/27, which is not a reduced residue.
All other entries checked (3–37, 43–71, 79, and 1/81, 2/81) are correct.

results.what: Table of decimal periods of a/p and a/p^k for p^k ≤ 81, one period per coset of <10> in (Z/p^k)^*, with numerators marked.
results.modern_name: Decimal period tables; cosets of the subgroup generated by 10; multiplicative order of 10 mod p
results.usually_credited_to: Gauss, Disquisitiones Arithmeticae (1801), arts. 312-318 and Table III. Earlier tables by Lambert, Robertson, Bernoulli and Hindenburg.

results.what: Observation that a period of a/N is a rotation of the period of 1/N exactly when a is congruent to a power of 10 mod N, and that the number of distinct periods is phi(N)/ord_N(10).
results.modern_name: Index of <10> in (Z/N)^*; Midy-type cyclic structure of repeating decimals

deep.surprise_reason: This is working material for, or an extension of, the decimal-fraction table published in Disquisitiones Arithmeticae Table III; Gauss's large tables are known (cf. Werke II). It is routine computation containing a few slips.
